source_snapshot.procedure: Generic setup says clear logs; open Hardware Status > Sensors and compare each sensor reading/setting with BMC sensor spec.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor reading and threshold are human readable and match specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES sends `TEMP_CPU0~1` as one literal name and truncates fallback output; it proves neither CPU population/socket mapping nor separate CPU0/CPU1 UI/spec fields.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION requires per-CPU topology, complete read-only records and separate evidence.

old_problem: Range notation was treated as a literal sensor operand and one response could be misreported as two-socket coverage. Actual socket population, BMC/BIOS/OS numbering, stable per-CPU sensors, threshold capability, load/freshness and separate WebUI rows were absent.
disposition_reason: The source intent is read-only per-sensor validation. Enumerate actual CPU population, map each populated physical socket through BIOS/BMC and OS/APIC identities to its own SDR/API and WebUI row, and evaluate every expected CPU independently. An unpopulated socket is N/A only with configuration proof; one/combined/average evidence never covers another socket. Exact topology/spec values are runtime prerequisites.
decision_basis: XLSX row 873, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, Script reference, selection manifest and historical record were directly reviewed.
`CPU0~1` is range notation, not a guaranteed IPMI wildcard or literal record name.
CPU numbering can differ across physical sockets, BIOS/BMC and OS/APIC, so topology join is required before field comparison.
ED-13 requires proof for unpopulated-socket N/A; ED-15 requires per-socket criteria; ED-17 rejects clearing; ED-20 forbids one socket substituting for another.

test_case.test_name: Verify each populated CPU0/CPU1 temperature sensor independently against topology and specification
test_case.purpose: Verify every populated CPU sensor represented by `TEMP_CPU0~1` is individually readable in Hardware Status > Sensors and has the correct physical socket/package identity, Celsius reading, units, health, implemented thresholds/hysteresis and freshness for the platform specification at the recorded passive load state.
required_package: Exact board/BIOS/BMC, fitted CPU model/stepping and physical socket-to-BMC/BIOS/OS/APIC package map
Stable SDR/API number/name/type/entity/instance and WebUI row for each expected populated CPU
Per-socket Celsius scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis and health/unavailable rules
Recorded host power/load/frequency state, BMC time, optional host package telemetry, update lag and approved delta
Pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual read-only method
test_case.test_command: Do not clear logs, add CPU stress, change power/fan policy or write thresholds. Inventory fitted sockets and build the physical/BIOS/BMC/OS numbering map. Enumerate the complete sensor repository; resolve separate stable CPU records for every populated socket instead of querying `TEMP_CPU0~1` literally. Review the Script before use. For each expected CPU independently capture full identity, value, units, capability/threshold/hysteresis, status and timestamp plus its matching WebUI row and recorded passive load state. Compare with the per-socket Project matrix and optional time-aligned host telemetry using approved scaling/lag/tolerance. Mark an absent socket N/A only from the approved population map; stop on swaps, duplicates, stale data or disagreement without retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every populated physical CPU socket has exactly one correctly mapped BMC sensor and WebUI row. Each independent record is readable, complete and agrees with its per-socket specification and approved freshness/tolerance; absent unpopulated sockets are explicitly proven N/A. No combined/average or other socket substitutes, and no logs/settings/load state are mutated.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the population/numbering map and separate complete OOB/UI/spec agreement for every populated socket with engineer verdict. A literal tilde query, one CPU, combined metric, average, truncated list or index assumption cannot pass. Missing/swapped/duplicate sensor, unjustified N/A, stale/out-of-tolerance value, required-threshold/status mismatch or mutation is FAIL. Missing topology/spec/reviewed method is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS; dynamic thermal behavior is not covered.
safety_gate: Do not query range notation literally or treat one/combined/average response as both CPUs.
Do not assume BMC index equals physical socket; bind entity metadata and platform topology.
Do not stress CPUs, alter fan/power settings or write thresholds.
Do not invent unsupported thresholds; N/A requires capability/population/spec proof.
Do not truncate output, expose credentials or run an unreviewed Script; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Board/BIOS/BMC, CPU models and physical socket-to-BMC/OS/package numbering matrix
Complete expected sensor inventory and separate per-CPU raw identity/value/unit/capability/threshold/status/timestamp records
Separate Hardware Status > Sensors evidence for every populated CPU
Per-socket Project matrix, passive load/power state and approved tolerance/update-lag comparison
Explicit absent/missing/duplicate/swapped disposition and pinned Script/alternate-method evidence
No-clear/no-write/no-stress/no-retry proof, health and engineer per-socket verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected. On mapping ambiguity, stale/mismatched values or unexpected health change, stop and preserve each socket's first evidence; use approved BMC/OS topology diagnostics without load injection or settings changes. Isolate any mutating Script and restore only through the authorized owner.

source_conflict.reason: The tilde is ambiguous as a command operand but the row consistently defines per-sensor read/spec validation; topology resolves execution identity.

blocked.reason: Per-CPU read-only validation is clear. Population, mapping and specifications are supplyable Project inputs.
